title: Geo Boundary Policy Hub: EU-restricted routing, tiered fallbacks, and customer allow/deny gates
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Implement a central 'Geo Boundary Policy Hub' in the routing layer that enforces EU-only data residency gates, supports per-customer allowlists/denylists, and orchestrates tier-aware fallback model variants when the preferred capacity is unavailable. Goals: (1) provide a single policy evaluator that takes customer configuration, request metadata, and global compliance rules to produce a deterministic route decision; (2) support explicit customer overrides (allowlists/denylists) with audit trails; (3) ensure graceful degradation by mapping to pre-approved model variants by tier (dedicated -> hosted compatible variant -> quantized fallback) while preserving residency constraints. This ticket covers the policy schema, runtime evaluator, integration hooks for the router, and rollout strategy including canarying and monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: Routing evaluator enforces EU-only residency for customers marked as 'eu_residency_required' and refuses to route outside EU regions unless an explicit, auditable customer allowlist exists.
Customer-level allowlist/denylist entries override default routing only when the configuration includes an approved justification and admin actor recorded in audit logs.

When preferred tier capacity is unavailable, router selects the correct fallback model variant according to policy mapping (preserves residency), and the request completes with documented fallback reason codes.
All routing decisions produce a structured audit record with fields: request_id, customer_id, policy_version, decision, rationale, resolved_region, resolved_model, and actor (if override).
End-to-end tests simulate cross-region failure and validate that EU customers never egress data to non-EU regions under default and allowlist-deny conditions.
Perf regression < 5% on 95th percentile latency for routing decision path under 5k rps with policy cache enabled.
Console UI shows per-customer routing policy summary and a timeline of recent routing decisions that can be filtered by reason code.
Security team completes the review and signs off the policy evaluator's threat model and audit retention plan.
implementation_notes:
Design: introduce a small, deterministic policy DSL (YAML/JSON) describing constraints: region_constraints, tier_preferences, allowlist/denylist blocks, and fallback_map. Implement a compact policy evaluator library in the router service (Go) with an in-memory policy cache and a persistence layer in config-store (etcd). Policy precedence: explicit customer denylist -> customer allowlist -> org-level residency constraint -> global defaults. For fallback mapping, use a model-variant registry that lists region compatibility and tier mapping; the evaluator must consult registry and capacity signals from the capacity plane. Add a 'decision_code' taxonomy for observability (OK, EU_RESTRICTION, ALLOW_OVERRIDE, DENY_OVERRIDE, FALLBACK_TIER, NO_CAPACITY, EGRESS_BLOCKED).

Runtime hooks: router calls evaluator with (customer_id, request_meta headers, model_hint, required_residency). Evaluator returns (resolve_region, model_variant, decision_code, audit_blob). Router logs the audit_blob to the audit sink and emits metrics: policy_decisions_total{decision_code}, decision_latency_ms, fallback_rate_by_tier.

Testing: unit tests for DSL parser and precedence rules, integration tests that spin up a sandbox capacity plane and simulate capacity loss, e2e tests with synthetic customers in EU and non-EU groups. Add mutation tests to ensure incorrect policies are rejected at upload time.

Migration: bulk-migration script to convert existing 'residency' flags to new policy objects; a compatibility layer to read legacy fields until all customers migrated. Backfill audit logs for last 90 days for customers flagged as 'eu_residency_required'.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary, 1% customers): Deploy evaluator behind feature-flag in router, enable policy cache, route only synthetic traffic and internal QA customers. Monitor decision metrics and audit log volume. Phase 2 (10% orgs): Open to a small set of pilot customers with EU residency needs; enable live routing but keep rollback ready. Phase 3 (GA): Flip feature flag for all customers after 2 weeks of stable metrics and security signoff. Provide a rollback toggle and emergency circuit-breaker that forces pre-policy behavior.
metrics_and_observability: Emit counters for decision_code and histograms for evaluation latency; record a per-request span with tags: customer_id, region_resolved, fallback_used, policy_version. Add dashboard: 'Geo Policy Decisions' showing top decision codes, per-customer fallback rates, and daily audit log ingestion size. Add alert: fallback_rate_by_tier > 2% sustained for 30m or decision_latency_p99 > 50ms.
security_considerations: Policy decisions are sensitive: do not include full request payloads in audit logs. Store audit blobs with only identifiers and hashed headers. Ensure audit sink supports customer-side retention controls for EU-residency customers and keys are managed via KMS. Mark this feature for mandatory security review and include threat model that covers malicious allowlist injection and replay attacks.
qa_notes: QA should run the e2e scenario matrix: (EU customer with dedicated capacity) x (dedicated up/down) x (allowlist present/absent) x (denylist present/absent) and validate outcomes. Validate audit logs contain actor and decision_code. Validate console UI shows policy summary and recent decisions for sample customers.
